name: Tether
desc: Issues USDT, the largest US-dollar stablecoin, and invests profits in bitcoin, AI and media companies.
capacity_detail: Valued at about USD 350bn (Feb 2026), per the unicorn list and cited Forbes article
markets: Worldwide USDT users outside the United States; planned US-domiciled stablecoin USAT; El Salvador base
rationale: Crypto exchanges and stablecoin rivals such as Circle, Coinbase and OKX already use F1 to build trust and global awareness.

name: DJI
desc: Makes consumer and professional drones, handheld gimbal cameras and action cameras sold in markets worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue CNY 80bn (USD 11.5bn) in 2025
markets: China, Japan, North America, Europe and Latin America divisions; over 90% of the global consumer drone market
rationale: Global camera and drone brand selling to filmmakers and enthusiasts; F1 broadcast and content production showcase aerial and onboard imaging.

name: Mistral AI
desc: Develops open-weight and commercial large language models and the Vibe assistant for businesses and consumers.
capacity_detail: Raised EUR 2bn at a EUR 12bn (about USD 14bn) valuation in Sep 2025
markets: European enterprises and governments, with partners including Microsoft, NVIDIA and Accenture; datacenters in France and Sweden

signals.raise: Samsung took a stake in a EUR 3bn transaction (Sep 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_AI)

rationale: European AI champion competing with Anthropic, Google and Microsoft, all F1 partners; F1 offers global B2B visibility.

name: Ola Consumer
desc: Indian ride-hailing app (formerly Ola Cabs) operated by ANI Technologies, offering cabs, autos and bikes.
capacity_detail: USD 500M round (Jul 2021) + USD 139M round (Dec 2021)
markets: More than 250 Indian cities; exited the UK, Australia and New Zealand in April 2024
rationale: Mass-market Indian mobility brand; F1's fast-growing Indian audience could support brand building, though spending is domestic.

name: Tenstorrent
desc: Designs RISC-V CPUs and AI inference accelerator chips, led by chip architect Jim Keller.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 1.5bn at a USD 6.2bn valuation (Oct 2026)
markets: Offices across the US, Canada, India, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Europe serving AI and chip customers
rationale: AI chip challenger to NVIDIA and AMD; AMD, Arm and Groq already use F1 for engineering-led B2B branding.

name: Toss (Viva Republica)
desc: Runs Toss, a South Korean financial super-app for payments, transfers, banking, investing and insurance.
capacity_detail: USD 80M round (2018) + USD 410M round (Jun 2021)
markets: South Korea, with over 20 million users, and Vietnam
rationale: Leading Korean fintech brand; rivals such as Revolut and Nu use F1 for consumer reach and international expansion.

name: CloudKitchens
desc: Leases delivery-only commercial kitchens to restaurants and food brands, led by Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick.
capacity_detail: USD 400M from PIF (2019) + USD 850M round (2021)
markets: United States, United Kingdom, Mexico, Colombia, Brazil and the Middle East
rationale: B2B real-estate operator with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could reach restaurant partners but fit is weak.

name: Sorare
desc: Fantasy sports game with licensed digital player cards for football, basketball and baseball.
capacity_detail: Series B USD 680M (Sep 2021) at a USD 4.3bn valuation
sponsorships: Licensing partnerships: La Liga (2021), MLB (2022), NBA (2022), Premier League (2023)
markets: Football, basketball and baseball fans worldwide on web, iOS and Android; regulatory focus on France and UK
rationale: Sports-licensing business model fits F1; a licensed F1 driver-card game would extend its fantasy portfolio.

name: Abnormal AI
desc: Sells AI-based email and collaboration security software that stops phishing and account takeover attacks.
capacity_detail: Series A USD 24M (2019) + USD 210M round (May 2022)
markets: Enterprises including more than 30% of the Fortune 500
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler and 1Password use F1 for enterprise awareness and hospitality with CISOs.

name: Branch
desc: Provides mobile deep-linking and attribution software that helps apps track and route users across channels.
capacity_detail: Rounds of USD 3M, 15M, 35M, 60M (2014-2017) + Series F USD 300M (Feb 2022)
markets: App developers and brands; only the US headquarters is stated
rationale: B2B marketing technology firm; F1 hospitality could reach app marketers, but brand-led fit is limited.

name: Articulate
desc: Makes Articulate 360 and Rise e-learning authoring software used by organisations to build employee training courses.
capacity_detail: USD 1.5bn round led by General Atlantic (Jul 2021)
markets: 125,000 organisations in 187 countries, including all of the Fortune 100
rationale: Enterprise software brand selling globally; Udemy and Workday use F1 to court corporate buyers.

name: Kurly
desc: Runs Market Kurly, a South Korean online grocery and beauty retailer with overnight cold-chain delivery.
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue KRW 2.3671 trillion (about USD 1.7bn) in 2025
markets: South Korea only, with logistics centres in Gimpo, Pyeongtaek and Changwon

signals.raise: Naver joined a capital increase (Jul 2026; https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/컬리_(기업))

rationale: Domestic consumer brand; F1 would mainly serve Korean awareness and premium positioning, so fit is limited.

name: ApplyBoard
desc: Online platform matching international students with colleges and universities abroad and handling their applications.
capacity_detail: Total funding of USD 475M raised as of 2021
markets: Students worldwide placed in Canada, the US, the UK, Ireland, Australia and Germany
rationale: Global education brand targeting young international audiences, though recent layoffs suggest limited marketing budget.

name: SpotOn
desc: Provides point-of-sale, payments and venue software for restaurants, retailers, stadiums and entertainment venues.
capacity_detail: Total of USD 628M raised including USD 300M Series E (Sep 2021)
markets: Restaurants and venues in the United States; its Appetize unit serves 65% of major league stadiums
rationale: Venue payments supplier; an F1 deal could showcase stadium and event technology to hospitality buyers.

name: Nuvemshop (Tiendanube)
desc: Latin American e-commerce platform that lets small and mid-sized brands build and run online stores.
capacity_detail: Series E USD 500M (Aug 2021); over USD 620M raised in the prior ten months
markets: Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Colombia and Chile, with over 180,000 merchant brands
rationale: Leading Latin American merchant platform; F1's strong Brazil and Mexico races offer direct regional brand exposure.

name: Bird (MessageBird)
desc: Cloud communications platform for SMS, WhatsApp, email and voice messaging used by businesses worldwide.
capacity_detail: First round USD 60M (2017) + Series C USD 200M (Oct 2020)
markets: Businesses in more than 150 countries across Europe, Asia and Latin America
rationale: B2B messaging brand competing with Infobip, already an F1 partner; F1 offers enterprise hospitality and visibility.

name: Veepee
desc: European online flash-sales retailer selling discounted fashion, home goods and travel from brand partners.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3.2bn in 2023
markets: France, Austria, Belgium, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland and Brazil
rationale: Large European consumer brand; F1's European races and fashion links could support brand partnerships and member acquisition.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: RigUp (Workrise)
desc: Provides contingent labour and vendor management software and services for oil, gas and energy companies.
capacity_detail: Total raised more than USD 750M including Series E USD 300M (May 2021)
markets: Upstream and midstream energy companies in the United States
rationale: US energy-services supplier; F1 hospitality might reach oil and gas clients, but consumer brand fit is weak.

name: BharatPe
desc: Indian fintech offering QR payments, card machines and loans to small merchants and shopkeepers.
capacity_detail: Series E of about USD 370M (2021), per sources cited on Wikipedia
markets: India, with more than 17 million merchant partners
rationale: Indian payments brand using cricket marketing; F1 is a minor fit given its domestic merchant focus.

name: Daangn (Karrot)
desc: Runs Daangn, a hyperlocal app for buying and selling second-hand goods among neighbours, branded Karrot abroad.
capacity_detail: Total raised USD 205M including Series D USD 162M (Aug 2021)
markets: South Korea, plus Karrot in Japan, Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom
rationale: Korean consumer app expanding abroad as Karrot; F1 could build awareness in new markets, but budgets look modest.

name: ManyPets
desc: Pet insurance provider, formerly Bought By Many, selling cover for cats and dogs online.
capacity_detail: Series D USD 350M led by EQT Growth (Jun 2021)
markets: Pet owners buying insurance online in the United Kingdom, Sweden and the United States
rationale: UK-led consumer insurer; F1's UK fan base suits awareness, though the category is rarely seen in F1.

name: PixVerse
desc: Develops an AI video generation app and platform that turns text and images into short videos.
capacity_detail: Valued at over USD 2bn after a USD 439M Series C extension (Jul 2026)
markets: Consumers and enterprises worldwide, with over 150 million registered users; offices in Singapore, Beijing and Shanghai

signals.raise: USD 439M Series C extension, valuation over USD 2bn (Jul 2026; https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/13/video-generation-startup-pixverse-raises-439m-valuation-soars-past-2b/)

rationale: Consumer AI creative brand chasing global users; F1 content and fans suit a video creation showcase.

name: Zerodha
desc: India's second-largest stockbroker, offering low-cost online trading in equities, derivatives, commodities and mutual funds.
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 8,847 crore (about USD 950M) in FY25
markets: India, as a member of NSE, BSE and MCX with 7.5 million active customers
rationale: Profitable trading brand; trading-app rivals eToro and Public use F1, but Zerodha avoids heavy advertising.

name: Trulioo
desc: Provides online identity and business verification services used by fintechs and payment firms to onboard customers.
capacity_detail: USD 394M financing (2021), of which about USD 150M went to the company
markets: Customers verifying identities across 181 countries, including Airwallex
rationale: Identity verification supplier to fintechs such as Airwallex, an F1 partner; B2B hospitality fit is moderate.

name: Cult.fit
desc: Runs Cult fitness centres, gyms, home workouts and fitness equipment in India.
capacity_detail: Total raised more than USD 670M, per its draft IPO filing
markets: India: 708 fitness centres in 77 cities, about 987,000 paid members

signals.ipo: Draft IPO prospectus filed with SEBI (Jul 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult.fit)

rationale: Fitness brand with a sport-adjacent identity; F1's growing Indian audience could support its pre-IPO profile.

name: Remote
industry: global payroll and employer of record
desc: Employer-of-record and payroll platform that lets companies hire and pay staff in other countries.
capacity_detail: Series A USD 35M (Nov 2020) + Series B USD 150M (Jul 2021)
markets: Employers hiring through its legal entities in 50+ countries
rationale: Global HR software brand; rivals UKG, Workday and Deel-type firms use sport for B2B awareness.

name: Hello (Hellobike)
desc: Chinese mobility company offering bike-sharing, e-scooters, battery swapping, ride-hailing and a robotaxi venture.
capacity_detail: Raised over USD 1.8bn across rounds since 2016
markets: Mainland China, plus HelloRide bike-sharing in Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Australia
rationale: Mobility brand expanding abroad with robotaxis; F1's Shanghai and Singapore races offer home and expansion exposure.

name: M1 Finance
desc: US investing and borrowing app with automated portfolios, managing over USD 14bn of client assets.
capacity_detail: Over USD 300M raised since 2015, including Series E USD 150M (Jul 2021)
markets: Retail investors and borrowers in the United States, with more than 400,000 clients
rationale: US trading-app brand; Public and Cash App already sponsor F1 teams to reach affluent American fans.

name: OneCard
desc: Indian fintech issuing app-based metal credit cards through partner banks, operated by FPL Technologies.
capacity_detail: Total raised over USD 225M, including Series D over USD 100M (Jul 2022)
markets: India, with credit cards issued through partner banks
rationale: Premium Indian card brand for young affluent users; F1 suits aspiration, but spending is domestic.
